text:
maya: Heads up — BrightLeaf on Dedicated pool 'eu-west-2-reserved' reporting sudden 429s after we applied their plan change earlier today. Support ticket #SL-7921. Error sample: "error: rate_limit_exceeded". Links: https://support.example/SL-7921

sanjay: thx maya. any timestamps / example request IDs? is this global or per-tenant?

maya: Request ID sample: req_0b3f2a, first seen 1723456702. Appears per-tenant: other tenants in same pool not affected in the same way but one noisy tenant had heavy short bursts earlier.

olivia: checked pool metrics — GPU utilization normal (30-45%), queue depth spiked for ~90s at 1723456695-1723456785. Autoscaler logs show a scale-up event but it lagged ~40s. ops-bot posted events: 
```
[ops-bot] 1723456720 autoscale: request to add node accepted -> provisioning
[ops-bot] 1723456760 autoscale: node ready
```

maya: customer says they were hitting 429s even before new node ready. Could be per-tenant rate window / burst ceilings misapplied. I captured a failing curl from their app: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-brightleaf" -H "X-Tenant-ID: brightleaf" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

sanjay: can you grab the routing key for req_0b3f2a from request logs? I want to see which rate key we computed. Also check if quota conversion happened at plan-change time. We recently changed a migration script that switches quota units to 'per-window' for dedicated pools.

maya: pasted routing/log lines: 
```
1723456702 req_0b3f2a tenant=brightleaf pool=eu-west-2-reserved rate_key=tenant:brightleaf:pool:eu-west-2-reserved window_seconds=60 applied_limit=120 burst_ceiling=60
```

olivia: aha — applied_limit=120 window_seconds=60 but burst_ceiling=60. That config means sustained 120/min but only 60 tokens allowed in an immediate burst. If their client did short rapid requests (many small calls), they can exhaust burst and get 429s until window replenishes. The noisy tenant earlier may have consumed pool-level shared burst budget causing spillover.

sanjay: also check the migration audit: I see an entry where config conversion used a default denom of 60 (seconds) for plans older than Feb-2025. Some legacy plans should have used 3600 instead. That would make a per-hour quota appear like per-minute -> effective throttle.

maya: searching: migration.log entry 1723456601 shows tenant brightleaf plan_id=pln-enterprise migrated units=3600 -> denom forced=60 by script #migrate-2025-11. That looks like the bug.

rachel: quick mitigation options: 1) bump burst_ceiling for brightleaf to match expected behavior (e.g., 600) and asynchronous rollout, 2) temporarily allow bucket refill grace for legacy-migrated tenants, 3) roll back migration change and re-run with correct denom mapping. Immediate safest: increase burst_ceiling for this tenant and record incident.

olivia: I'm worried about noisy neighbor side-effects if we blindly increase burst for everyone. Let's do tenant-scoped change for BrightLeaf only and add telemetry to detect repeat. I'll patch rate-mapper to treat flagged legacy plans as per-hour unless explicitly set.

sanjay: agree. rca steps: identify all tenants that hit this migration path, compare their historical token rates, and run a bulk correction job. For right-now fix: maya, can you set brightleaf.burst_ceiling=600 via admin API and confirm?

maya: doing now... admin call: 
```
POST /admin/tenants/brightleaf/config
{ "burst_ceiling": 600 }
```

ops-bot: 
```
1723456930 admin-api: tenant brightleaf updated burst_ceiling=600 by maya
```

maya: after change, customer reports errors dropped, last 10m sample shows 0 429s for brightleaf. They confirm app-level retries back to normal. :thumbsup:

olivia: will schedule a batch correction script and add a safety check to the migration job. Also adding a metric alert for mismatch of window_seconds vs plan-denom.

sanjay: please capture repro steps and commands used (curl, admin api) in the ticket and tag eng-runtime for follow-up. We should also instrument per-tenant burst depletion traces so we can correlate noisy neighbors to burst pool spillover.

maya: added notes + logs to SL-7921 and flagged eng-runtime. Closing the immediate customer escalation. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:

rachel: follow-up tasks: ENG-2331 (fix migration denom), ENG-2332 (per-tenant burst telemetry), OPS-981 (playbook for tenant-scoped emergency bump). I'll assign and ping owners.

maya: marking thread resolved for support. If anyone wants the log snippets I can paste into the ticket.

sanjay: nice catch. TL;DR: migration introduced denom mismatch -> per-hour quotas were interpreted as per-minute -> burst ceiling too small -> 429s during short bursts + autoscale lag made it worse. Tenant-scoped bump fixed immediate issue.

olivia: adding :incident: note and closing ops loop.
